ai.title: Anthropic Releases FlashProve: Cryptographic Proofs That a Reply Came From Committed Weights
ai.brief: Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team has released FlashProve , an open-source research prototype for provable inference . FlashProve is a zkSNARK system from Anthropic that proves a reply came from a committed model. The proof reveals nothing about the model weights. On Llama 4 Maverick , a 400B mixture-of-experts model, it proves about 110 tokens/second on 1 H100. For developers, this targets a real gap: today you cannot check which model actually answered your API call. TL;DR Size: Proves a 400B MoE model (~17B active per token); context capped at 1,024 tokens per request. Runs on: Prover needs 1 H100 80 GB, 24 CPU cores and ~290 GB host RAM. Verifier runs on a CPU, no GPU. Performance: Orders of magnitude faster than prior open-source zkML systems on the same 400B model. 78 MB proofs checked in 17 seconds.

sec.title: Binance Hack: How Fake Job Interviews and AI Abuse Led to a $6.34 Billion Attack
sec.brief: S. S. 3 Billion Stolen from Binance in Attack Attributed to North Korea The Binance security incident on October 29 shows how a fake recruitment process can become the entry point to critical financial infrastructure. The attackers combined social engineering, compromised developer tools, stolen credentials and abuse of an internal AI application to reach the cryptocurrency exchange’s wallet signing systems.
